card.summary: 0.5 GB of data storage on a shared cluster with three-node replication, one free cluster per project, free forever

free_tier.stated: 0.5 GB of data storage on a shared cluster with three-node replication, one free cluster per project, free forever

per_object_cap.stated: 16 mebibytes per BSON document, which is the MongoDB engine limit and not a tier limit

retention.stated: paused automatically after 30 days with zero connections; resumable unless the cluster ran a version Atlas can no longer restore to

egress.terms: 10 GB in and 10 GB out per rolling seven-day period; exceeding it throttles the cluster and adds a one-second cooldown per connection

record.interface_detail: the MongoDB wire protocol; a Data API for HTTPS access; the Atlas Administration API and the atlas CLI
record.tooling: mongosh, any MongoDB driver, the atlas CLI
record.chaining: a free document store that survives inactivity for a month, which is the longest idle clock in this class short of Aiven

limits.value: 100 operations per second, enforced by throttling with a one-second cooldown
0.5 GB of data storage; storage size is not configurable on a free cluster
10 GB in and 10 GB out per rolling 7-day period
paused after 30 days with zero connections

record.limits_note: 500 connections maximum; replication factor 3; no sharding, no network peering, and only a subset of regions

identity_cost.detail: an Atlas account; no card on Free

record.reliability_note: the page is explicit that Atlas may deactivate idle free clusters under its terms, and recommends exporting a copy before a long pause
record.confidence_note: both pages were read on 2026-10-22: the Atlas free-tier limits page for the 0.5 GB, the pause and the throttles, and the server limits page for the 16 mebibyte document cap. The storage figure is 0.5 GB as the page states it. 512 MB is the binary rendering of the same quantity and is not a second figure.

evidence.proved: 'Free clusters: 0.5 GB' for Data Storage; 'Atlas automatically pauses Free clusters after 30 days of inactivity where there are zero connections'; 10 GB in and out per rolling seven-day period; 100 operations per second; 500 connections; 'You can't configure storage size for Free clusters'
'The maximum BSON document size is 16 mebibytes', which is an engine limit and not an Atlas tier limit

record.notes: 0.5 GB is a hard wall rather than an overage, and 100 ops/s is a throughput cap that no storage allowance can exceed. The 30-day idle clock is the most forgiving in this class and it is still a clock.

card.summary: 512 MB data storage per free cluster (0.5 GB, uncompressed BSON + indexes); one free cluster per project; 250 projects per Atlas user and 250 per organization

free_tier.stated: 512 MB data storage per free cluster (0.5 GB, uncompressed BSON + indexes); one free cluster per project; 250 projects per Atlas user and 250 per organization

egress.terms: Data transfer out is not the metered axis on M0. There is no published egress allowance or overage for Free clusters; the limits that bite are 500 connections and 100 ops/sec. Effectively unmetered for read volume, which makes M0 unusual in this class.

record.tooling: Standard MongoDB drivers (pymongo, motor), `mongosh`, Atlas Data API (HTTPS), `mongodump`/`mongorestore`; GridFS for files >16 MB via pymongo's gridfs
record.chaining: 250 projects per user x 1 free cluster each x 512 MB = ~128 GB per Atlas account, and 250 organizations per user gives another axis. GridFS chunks (255 KB default) mean no practical per-object cap beyond the 512 MB total.
record.limits_note: 512 MB total is tiny per unit. The whole value is the 250x multiplier. 100 ops/sec, 500 connections, no sharding, no configurable storage. Cluster creation is heavily rate-limited in practice (one free cluster per project, project creation itself throttled).
record.reliability_note: Free clusters are shared and throttle at 100 ops/sec; a bulk-write workload will be visibly slow rather than failing. Data is 3-node replicated, no vanishing.

evidence.proved: 'Free clusters: 0.5 GB ... all uncompressed BSON documents ... plus the bytes stored in their associated indexes'; 'only one Free cluster per project'
'Projects per Atlas User | 250', 'Projects per Atlas Organization | 250'
